title: Capital Agent Sanitized Signal
description: Shape of data the Editorial Platform is allowed to hand back to the Capital Agent (prompt-evolucao-subsistema-editorial.md §21-22). This is an export contract, not a database - nothing here implies shared storage or a runtime dependency. Every field is either a pseudonymous id, an aggregate number, or a controlled category tag. No name, email, phone, raw message, or any other individually-identifying data has a place in this schema by design; the closed additionalProperties list is the enforcement, not just documentation.

signal_id.description: Pseudonymous id for this export event. Never a lead id, session id, or anything traceable back to an individual on the Capital Agent side.

signal_type.description: Which of the three things §21 says the Editorial Platform may return. Nothing else is in scope for this export - no draft content, no plan internals, no CMS credentials.

experiment_id.description: Capital Agent's own experiment identifier, echoed back so it can correlate - this repo never assigns or interprets it, only carries it through.

attribution_tags.description: Controlled category tags only (e.g. 'organic-search', 'referral-linkedin') - never a raw referrer URL with query parameters, never a user agent string.

aggregate_metrics.description: Same aggregate-only rule as editorial/schema/outcome.schema.json#/properties/metrics. A count small enough to identify an individual (e.g. qualified_leads: 1 for a niche page) is a real re-identification risk even though the field itself is 'just a number' - see the accepted-limitation note in the work item; no k-anonymity threshold is enforced yet.
